title: 2001 HMMT February Guts Problem 10
statement: Two concentric circles have radii \(r\) and \(R>r\). Three new circles are drawn so that they are each tangent to the big two circles and tangent to the other two new circles. Find \(\frac{R}{r}\).

solutions.text: The centers of the three new circles form a triangle. The diameter of the new circles is \(R-r\), so the side length of the triangle is \(R-r\). Call the center of the concentric circle \(O\), two vertices of the triangle \(A\) and \(B\), and \(A B\) 's midpoint \(D\). \(O A\) is the average \(R\) and \(r\), namely \(\frac{R+r}{2}\). Using the law of sines on triangle \(D A O\), we get \(\frac{\sin (30)}{A D}=\frac{\sin (90)}{A O} \Rightarrow R=3 r\), so \(\frac{R}{r}=3\).
